restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM; total computation summed across all processors; one five-round sponge permutation = one unit and every other primitive 256-bit word operation = 1/C with C=1355.

Complete fixed-IV SHA3-256: all-zero 1600-bit state, rate 1088, capacity 512, suffix 0x06 then pad10*1, prefix rounds 0..4 with original round constants in every permutation, full 256-bit digest. Rate, capacity, suffix, IV, round range and output length are unchanged.
Ordinary full collision of the complete SHA3-256 hash; NOT a raw-permutation distinguisher, free-start/compression-only collision, near-collision, or reduced-capacity (c=160) contest instance.

Dedicated five-round attack by conditional internal differentials: an improved-TIDA connector over the first two rounds (reached by ~2^25 first-block trials), a 3.5-round conditional internal-differential characteristic (Characteristic 3 of the paper's Section 6.3) with transition condition numbers (k2,k3,k4)=(21,18,16) that the paper states applies identically to SHA3-256, and a variant birthday search over disjoint collision subsets. Two-block messages; degrees of freedom of the initial message space >= 540.
For output length d=256 the collision is placed on the first five lanes before the last chi, which propagates to equal first-320 output bits and hence a full 256-bit digest collision.

Published all-in total time complexity for d=256 is 2^105 (Zhang-Hou-Liu, EUROCRYPT 2023, Table 5; the Section 6.3 formula 2^(A+(m+16)/2), A already covering connector oversampling and Stage-2 rejection, verified against the paper's d=384 case 2^(18+(224+16)/2)=2^138); corroborated by Dinur-Dunkelman-Shamir FSE 2013 (2^115) and by the real five-round SHA3-256 collision of Guo et al., J. Cryptology 2020.

Conservative charge: the paper's all-in 2^105 doubled to 2^106 (no-early-stop/full-pool convention) + sorting/lookup < 2^103 + connector slack <= 2^80, total < 2^106.01; claimed time_log2 = 106.5 is a strict upper bound (F-COST-1).

Analytic complexity bound with infeasible work and large memory; no colliding pair is exhibited (a witness would be rejected and the claim is deliberately analytic). Success probability >= 0.5 for the stated budget is the algorithmic success event; it is separate from the epistemic status of the declared heuristic.

heuristics.statement: The 3.5-round conditional internal-differential characteristic with transition condition numbers (k2,k3,k4)=(21,18,16), connected deterministically to the SHA3-256 initial state by the improved target internal difference algorithm, partitions the 2^106 constructed inputs into disjoint collision subsets on which the map through the final rounds behaves as a random function; consequently the variant-birthday argument of Zhang-Hou-Liu (EUROCRYPT 2023, Eqs. 2-5) returns a full 256-bit five-round SHA3-256 collision with probability >= 0.5 at input count N=2^106 (reported complexity 2^105). This is the standard working premise of internal-differential collision cryptanalysis of Keccak/SHA-3.
heuristics.scope: Five-round SHA3-256, capacity 512, output 256 bits, prefix rounds 0..4 with original round constants; the specific 3.5-round characteristic (k2,k3,k4)=(21,18,16) and output length d=256 with the collision taken on the first five lanes before the last chi.
heuristics.extrapolation: The same technique lineage (generalized internal differentials of Dinur-Dunkelman-Shamir, FSE 2013, giving 2^115 for this target) is empirically confirmed at lower rounds: EUROCRYPT 2023 reports that for its three-round instance the observed number of colliding subsets matched the theoretical value, and Guo et al. (J. Cryptology 2020) exhibit an actual five-round SHA3-256 colliding pair. The 2^105 five-round figure is the peer-reviewed theoretical estimate obtained by this characteristic; we charge 2^106.5 as a strict upper bound over it.
heuristics.limitations: The five-round complexity is a theoretical estimate backed by peer review and by corroborating practical/near-scale results, not machine-reproduced at full five-round scale in this package. It assumes the random-function-within-subset behaviour standard to internal-differential cryptanalysis. It concerns only the five-round prefix variant and implies nothing about full 24-round SHA3-256.
